_status: VERIFIED 2026-05-21 — USPSTF grades retrieved from primary source (see _provenance). Pre-2002 START point is a clinical-practice stance, NOT a USPSTF letter grade — flagged below.
_provenance: USPSTF recommendation history for HORMONE THERAPY for the PRIMARY PREVENTION OF CHRONIC CONDITIONS in postmenopausal persons (NOT symptom treatment). Grade D ('recommends against') for combined estrogen+progestin since the 2002 statement (post-WHI E+P arm) and for estrogen-alone since 2005 (post-WHI estrogen-only arm); grade D reaffirmed 2012, 2017, 2022. Sources: 2012 archived statement https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/menopausal-hormone-therapy-preventive-medication-2012 ; 2022 final statement https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/document/RecommendationStatementFinal/menopausal-hormone-therapy-preventive-medication (JAMA 2022, PMID 36318127) ; 2002 statement Ann Intern Med 2002 https://www.acpjournals.org/doi/10.7326/0003-4819-137-10-200211190-00013 ; evidence review NBK97829 https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK97829/ . The USPSTF history block lists prior versions Dec 2017, Oct 2012, Jan 2002, Jan 1996. The 1996 statement used the older I/II/III evidence framework (USPSTF adopted A-D/I letters in 1998) so it carries NO comparable letter grade [UNCONFIRMED]; the pre-2002 START point below encodes the documented pre-WHI clinical-practice stance (HRT widely recommended for CVD/chronic-disease prevention, per NBK97829), NOT a USPSTF letter grade.
_mapping_note: USPSTF grade D ('recommends against using HRT for prevention') maps to strong agreement with these anti-HRT-for-prevention claims -> direction SUPPORTS, level strong-for. The USPSTF grade is for the OVERALL recommendation; the per-claim direction/level here is a faithful interpretation onto each atomic claim, not a separate USPSTF grade per sub-claim. Claims (from the eval input) are phrased in the modern against-HRT direction: claim-1='HRT should not be used for chronic-disease prevention', claim-2='no net cardiovascular prevention benefit', claim-3='harms outweigh prevention benefits'. Pre-WHI the field believed the opposite -> those claims were REFUTED then.
scope_note: HRT for chronic-disease prevention; the documented 180-degree reversal: pre-2002 HRT recommended for CVD/chronic-disease prevention -> WHI 2002/2005 RCTs -> USPSTF grade D recommends against, sustained through 2022.

claim-1._basis: pre-WHI clinical-practice stance (HRT recommended for prevention) -> the should-not-use claim is refuted; NOT a USPSTF letter grade
USPSTF grade D (2002 E+P, 2005 estrogen-alone, 2012 D) recommends against use

claim-2._basis: pre-WHI belief that HRT confers net cardiovascular benefit
WHI showed no net CV prevention benefit; USPSTF grade D

claim-3._basis: pre-WHI: harms not believed to outweigh prevention benefits
WHI: excess stroke/thromboembolism; harms outweigh prevention benefits; USPSTF grade D
